subject: Latency spike — request for incident audit artifacts and retention details
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finlogix.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-04T16:12:00Z
Subject: Services degraded this morning — high latency + 500s

Hi Sean,

We saw a sustained latency spike and an increase in 500 responses across our account between 09:05 and 09:47 PDT this morning. Impacted endpoints appear to be the text-generation route (v2) and embeddings; throughput was about 40% of expected and error rate spiked to ~6%. This caused timeouts in our ingestion pipeline and a downstream batch job failure.

We need two things ASAP: an incident timeline for affected requests and confirmation about what logs you can provide for debugging (request IDs, full request/response latencies, and whether logs include any input payloads). Also, our security/compliance lead asked for evidence that no customer PII was retained beyond our configured retention window — can you confirm that and tell us how you will share artifacts?

Liam
Liam O'Connor
SRE, FinLogix
liam.oconnor@finlogix.com

Attachment: incident_kpi_screenshot.png (image of Grafana spikes)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finlogix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-04T16:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Services degraded this morning — high latency + 500s

Liam — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. We’re treating this as a P1 for FinLogix and have already started collecting diagnostics.

Quick answers up front:
- We can provide per-request logs (request ID, timestamps for queue/served/tokens, and response status).
- Raw request payloads are included in the application logs for the time window by default; we can provide a sanitized extract if you prefer no raw inputs.
- Retention: your account is configured for 30-day retention for request logs; I'll confirm the retention policy and whether any manual exports were created.

I’m looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Rishi (infra) to coordinate artifacts and timeline. Can you confirm the earliest and latest sample request IDs you’re concerned about (or a narrower timestamp range)? Also indicate whether you require an encrypted transmit (SFTP/secure drive) for artifacts.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Enterprise Success | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Team — forwarding FinLogix's escalation (see below). They want: (1) per-request timeline and request IDs, (2) confirmation about whether payloads are present in logs, and (3) evidence about retention & no-PII assertions.

Action items:
- Rishi: pull the raw logs for 2026-06-04T16:50Z - 2026-06-04T17:00Z UTC (corresponding to their 09:05-09:47 PDT window) and produce: request-level CSV (request_id, route, status, latency_ms, start_ts, end_ts) and a sample of full request payloads for 50 requests. Place the artifacts in a secure bucket and flag any records with potential PII.
- Grace: confirm what we can share / redaction approach and whether sharing the raw payloads requires a DPA addendum for this export. Also provide SOC 2 control references we can point FinLogix to.
- Marissa: coordinate the customer communication; keep Liam apprised of timelines and provide an encrypted link for delivery.

We should aim to get a first artifacts pack to the customer within 6 hours. Looping in Aditya for visibility since this is a VP-level escalation on their side.

Thanks — Sean

Sean / Marissa — I pulled the initial artifacts and started a sanitization pass. Notes:
- Raw logs (application + access) for the requested window are available and I staged a tarball: redwood_raw_logs_20260604.tgz (contains request level JSONs).
- I generated request-level CSV with columns: request_id, model, route, status, latency_ms, start_ts, end_ts. Early look: we see a correlated increase in queueing latency starting at ~2026-06-04T16:58Z UTC. 500s correlate with a transient upstream timeout in our autoscaler path for a specific shard.
- The raw JSONs include request inputs. Per our standard procedure, those are retained for 30 days. If FinLogix wants sanitized versions we can redact input text fields (replace with [REDACTED]) or provide a hash map (sha256 of inputs) for verification without sharing content.

Timeline for delivery:
- Secure bucket with CSV and initial summary: in 45 minutes (2026-06-04T18:30Z).
- Full tarball with raw JSONs (encrypted): in 2 hours.
- Sanitized payload extract (50 samples): 2.5 hours.

I flagged any entries that appear to have long inputs (likely customer uploads) and will provide a separate list if needed.

-Rishi

Attachment: redwood_raw_logs_20260604.tgz (staged, encrypted)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-04T18:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Services degraded this morning — high latency + 500s

Thanks team — security notes for sharing: 
- SOC 2 mapping: we can provide the control narratives relevant to logging and retention (CC6.1, CC7.3) as part of the pack.
- PII: the application logs may contain user-provided text. We cannot assert "no PII" without checking content. Recommend providing both: (a) sanitized extracts (text fields redacted) and (b) hashes of the original inputs (sha256) so the customer can verify that the sanitized set corresponds to the originals without seeing raw content.
- Transfer: use the secure bucket link with client-side encryption or an SFTP exchange. Do not send raw JSONs over email.
- Audit evidence: we will include (i) retention policy snapshot (policy id RP-30D), (ii) access log snippet showing who exported the data and when, and (iii) a signed statement from Security describing redaction steps.

I'll prepare the SOC 2 references and the signed statement. Let me know if FinLogix requires a formal DPA amendment for this export — if they do, route it to Legal.

—Grace
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Incident artifacts and security controls — FinLogix incident (June 4)

Hi Liam / Sasha —

Thanks again for the patience. Below is what we will deliver to FinLogix and the planned timelines:

Delivered / Attached: 
- redwood_raw_logs_20260604.tgz (encrypted) — complete request JSONs for 2026-06-04T16:50Z through 2026-06-04T17:00Z UTC.
- request_timeline_FLX_DL-9832.csv — per-request summary (request_id, route, status, latency_ms, start_ts, end_ts).
- incident_kpi_screenshot.png (from your monitoring) — included for context.
- secure_share_instructions.txt — how to access the secure bucket and verify checksums.

Security & compliance notes: 
- Retention: your account retention setting is RP-30D (30 days). We have not modified retention for FinLogix; I attached a signed retention policy snapshot and an audit log snippet showing the export activity (who/when).
- PII handling: the raw request JSONs may contain customer-provided text input. Per Grace's recommendation, we included a sanitized sample set (50 records) with text fields redacted and corresponding sha256 hashes so you can confirm mapping to originals without seeing raw inputs.
- Transfer method: artifacts placed in a client-isolated secure bucket; delivery is encrypted at rest and in transit. We provided both SFTP credentials and the secure Drive link in the instructions file.

Next steps:
- Please confirm receipt and whether you want additional sanitization.
- If Legal needs a DPA amendment or a formal attestation for the export, loop in your counsel and we'll coordinate.

I’m keeping Aditya and the account team informed due to the executive escalation on your side. If you'd like, we can run a short post-incident review this week to walk through root cause and mitigations for throughput and autoscaler behavior.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Enterprise Success | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
